title: 'Flock Flocked up'

reading.body:
This is a false-positive match in an automated licence plate reader, and the failure propagated into a physical, armed police response. The system flagged a plate as stolen, but the vehicle it was attached to did not match the vehicle the system associated with that plate. The mismatch was between a Chevy Malibu and a red Dodge Ram pickup, which is the kind of discrepancy a human reviewer comparing the alert image against the vehicle in front of them could have caught before the stop escalated. The stop, the drawn guns, the K-9 release and the arrest all followed from an alert that was wrong at the point it was issued.

The failure sits at the handoff between an automated alert and the officers acting on it. Nothing in the reporting shows that anyone verified the alert against the vehicle before the stop began, and the officers' stated concern about flight or weapons is a separate judgement made after the stop was already under way. Catching this would have required a check at the moment of the alert, comparing the flagged vehicle against the one actually present, rather than treating the alert as a settled fact. The reporting also notes that multiple officers are under investigation over the K-9 release, and that the department's own investigation found no wrongdoing in that release.

What is not established is whether the camera's misread was a known limitation, whether any policy required verification before a stop, or what discipline or further action may follow. An internal finding of no wrongdoing is not a finding that the alert was correct, and an investigation is not a conclusion.

reports.title: Body cam of TPD officers releasing K-9 on man during traffic stop
Man speaks out after police release K-9 on him during traffic stop: 'Traumatized'
TPD investigation finds no wrongdoing in use of K-9 on man during traffic stop
Charges dropped against man Toledo Police released K-9 on during traffic stop, lawyer says

summary:
Toledo Police released body camera video showing officers drawing guns and using a K-9 on a driver during a traffic stop. The stop began after a FLOCK camera alert about a stolen plate, but the alert was wrong. The camera image matched a Chevy Malibu while the plate was actually on a red Dodge Ram pickup. The driver, Brandon Upchurch, got out with his hands up, then walked toward the grass. He was arrested and charged with resisting arrest and obstruction, and police later confirmed the plate was not stolen.

Officers said they thought Upchurch might flee and did not know if he or his passenger had weapons. He received medical attention at the scene. Multiple TPD officers are under investigation over the K-9 release. The article does not say what discipline or further action may follow.
